crash: C++ize anomaly detector and have it use the journal Have anomaly_detector use the systemd journal as its log source instead of reading from /var/log/messages. Audit messages have been moved to /var/log/audit/audit.log, and attempts to make anomaly_detector read two files proved complicated: https://crrev.com/c/1630336 It was cleaner to completely rewrite anomaly detector by migrating it to C++ than to try to fit the current unit tests with the journal implementation. This has the added advantage of reducing the dependencies of the unit test and making it much faster since we no longer need to repeatedly call sleep. It's also now understood by the unit test framework as a group of multiple tests instead of one big test. Reading from journal has several advantages, most of which we aren't taking advantage of in this change, but can done in the future. Possible future improvements: * Use sd_journal_add_match and friends to make following the journal more efficient. * Save the journal cursor between boots to avoid missing certain early-boot and shutdown crashes: https://crbug.com/343954#c8 * Leverage structured audit data. Journald actually has all the audit fields we parse from the audit line as structured data. Use these instead of parsing the audit line. Introduce power.WilcoPeakShift The Peak Shift policy on Wilco devices uses the EC to schedule when the DUT uses AC power. Specifically, by using the policy it is possible to schedule 3 different modes: - Use AC and charge the battery (max AC usage) - Use AC, but don't charge the battery (medium AC usage) - Don't use AC, and run off just the battery. (no AC usage) For more information, see https://www.chromium.org/administrators/policy-list-3#DevicePowerPeakShiftEnabled In order to test all aspects of the policy, it must be possible for the EC to charge the battery. That would require the battery level to be less than 100%, but since in the lab all devices are always plugged into AC, the batteries are kept at 100%. In order to test the charging behavior this test would need to drain the batteries somewhat, which could take ~10 minutes. Therefore, this test only verifies that the device can toggle AC usage on and off, and doesn't test for battery charging/no-charging. TODO(b/138940522): Add a more thorough, slower, manual test for all aspects of the policy. Also, the EC currently takes a minute to update its behavior after a policy change. This mean this test has a timeout of 4 minutes, but from test runs it usually takes about 2.5 minutes. I've filed a bug to try to fix this at b/138612166. cryptohome: Add new commandline features for cryptohome commandline tool. To add new data restore key, simply type: cryptohome --action=add_data_restore_key --user=your_user_name Then type in your password, wait for a few second, then the hex string of data restore key will be displayed if authenticated. To build authentication, testers can use switch "--restore_key_in_hex" to provide data restore key in HexString, for instance if testers type: cryptohome --action=check_key_ex --user=your_user_name --restore_key_in_hex=0123456789ABCDEF Cryptohome will use restore key in AuthorizationRequest and check if it can be authenticated. To mass remove keys, users need to provide exempt key labels. Every other keyset whose label is not in exempt_key_labels will be removed. For instance, if users have four keysets which are labeled as "l1", "l2", "l3" and "l4", say if they want to delete l1 and l2 and keep l3 and l4, they should type: cryptohome --action=mass_remove_keys --user=your_user_name --exempt_key_labels=l3,l4 After authenticated, l1 and l2 will be removed.
